references.title: Galileo Galilei, Dialogues Concerning Two New Sciences (1914 English translation)
references.support: Primary-text evidence: in the First Day, Salviati contrasts the declining proportion of squares in finite ranges with every number being a root of a square, then says equal/greater/less comparisons do not apply to infinite quantities. Consulted in the Crew and de Salvio 1914 translation; this does not establish that Galileo used later cardinality terminology.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Infinity
references.support: Scholarly historical and philosophical reference supporting the account of Galileo’s paradox, the later Cantorian cardinality criterion and the distinct cardinalities of the positive integers and reals; also describes later numerosity approaches. Consulted relevant archived sections; secondary synthesis, not primary testimony.

references.title: Matthew W. Parker, “Philosophical Method and Galileo’s Paradox of Infinity”
references.support: Scholarly philosophical-historical analysis offering one interpretation of the paradox as involving distinct concepts of number and size, and treating Cantorian cardinality as a useful but not uniquely correct extension. Relevant chapter passages were consulted; this is not presented as consensus.
